title: EIA Weekly Petroleum Status Report — US crude, gasoline and distillate stocks for the week ending 2026-09-18 (10:30 ET, flash-PMI morning, the first full data week of the Petroline outage)
source: EST: eia.gov/petroleum/supply/weekly/schedule.php, re-fetched direct 2026-09-16 (HTTP 200, 51,258 bytes) and read from its own markup. It states verbatim that the summary, overview and Tables 1-14 in CSV/XLS are released 'after 10:30 a.m. eastern time on Wednesday', and its Holiday Release Schedule names 2026 exceptions ONLY for the weeks ending 01-16, 02-13, 05-22, 09-04, 10-09 and 11-06. The week ending 2026-09-18 is not among them, so the standard rule applies unmodified; 2026-09-23 is a Wednesday and 2026-09-18 is the Friday five days before it. TWO REASONS THIS IS `estimate`, NEITHER OF THEM DATE DOUBT: (1) the date is DERIVED from the publisher's stated cadence plus weekday arithmetic, not read off a dated row — eia.gov/petroleum/supply/weekly/ (fetched direct 2026-09-16, HTTP 200, 70,853 bytes) still names only 'Data for week ending Sep. 4, 2026 / Release Date: Sep. 10, 2026 / Next Release Date: Sep. 16, 2026', and will not name 09-23 until the 09-16 release publishes later the same day; (2) market-events-data.ts's confirmed-prefix taxonomy defines NO `EIA:` prefix (IR:/CAL:/BLS:/FED:/PJM:/SEC:/TSY:/OCC:/BEA:/CENSUS:/ISM:/CB:/UMICH:/FHFA:), the same schema gap eia-weekly-petroleum-status-2026-09-16, -2026-09-30 and every eia-steo-* entry record — adding one would confirm this whole class and is a schema change, not this lane's call. Checked 2026-09-16
notes: CANONICAL FILE WRITTEN BY THIS EVENT'S OWN never-assessed INITIAL RESEARCH, 2026-09-16 (D-7), after reading the one proposal that named this id — proposals/eia-weekly-petroleum-status-2026-09-23.from-sp-global-flash-us-pmi-2026-09-23.json, filed by the flash-PMI lane the same day. That proposal's ATTRIBUTION rationale is adopted unchanged: 10:30 ET is 45 minutes after the 09:45 ET flash-PMI window closes, so naming this print CONFIRMS rather than voids that lane's clean-window claim. THE INITIAL RESEARCH ADDS TWO REASONS THE PROPOSAL DID NOT HAVE, both measured. (1) TURNAROUND, EARLY: 2026-09-23 reports the week ending 09-18, exactly 14 days past the 97.8% utilization printed for the week ending 09-04. Across 1993-2025 the +14d analog declined in 23 of 33 years, in 6 of 6 when the base was >= 96.0 and in 3 of 3 when it was >= 97.0 (1997 -0.9, 1998 -2.4, 2018 -7.2, median -2.40); two convergent point estimates land at 95.4 and 95.9. But at +14d only 1 of the 3 high-base analogs printed BELOW 96.0, against 2 of 3 at the +21d offset the 09-30 sibling studied — so the DECLINE is robust here and the LEVEL is not, and this ledger deliberately does not re-use the sibling's 96.0 threshold. (2) THE ARB, NOT THE NARRATIVE: the Brent-WTI futures spread has compressed from a pre-attack 6-month mean of 5.38 to a post-09-10 mean of 4.31 and 3.26 in the 2026-09-16 overnight session — the WRONG direction for a US export pull, in the middle of a supply shock everyone reads as bullish crude. Measured over 2021-2026, the spread leads US crude exports best at a THREE-week lag (corr +0.417; +0.274 on 2023+ alone), which maps this print's week back to the week ending 08-28's wide 6.21 — so the compression bites the EARLY-OCTOBER prints, not this one. NO PRICE CHANNEL IS CLAIMED and impact is tiered low deliberately: no house playbook is energy-keyed, no tracked symbol carries direct crude exposure, and `symbols` is EMPTY on purpose. Context at writing (2026-09-15 22:48 ET): CL=F 104.74, BZ=F 108.10, HO=F 4.9797, RB=F 3.2344, XLE 65.93, USO 161.86, XOP 199.70, VIX 17.20. Full ledger with sources: docs/research/events/eia-weekly-petroleum-status-2026-09-23.md. Estimate widens caution only; it licenses no date-keyed action.
